title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: A long-term academic pathway combining environmental, energy and climate law research, teaching, publications, grants and institutional leadership.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap treats 2026 as the starting point and uses research-stage years rather than assuming that a Ph.D. is completed within a fixed number of years. Faculty recruitment, promotion and research requirements must be checked against the rules applicable when you apply.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build a defensible environmental/energy/climate-law research profile, publish consistently, gain teaching experience and develop a recognisable doctoral specialisation.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Postdoctoral/faculty-stage specialisation in areas such as climate governance, energy transition, environmental regulation or climate litigation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Become an independent researcher, supervisor and grant-holder with a sustained publication programme and institutional responsibilities.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine scholarship, postgraduate supervision, policy engagement and academic leadership while tracking new climate, energy and environmental regulation.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Maintain one deep research identity while adding emerging subjects such as carbon markets, climate finance, energy-storage regulation, AI and environmental governance, climate adaptation, biodiversity governance and just-transition law. blocks.label: Career progression
blocks.text: Ph.D. Researcher (2026–2030±) → Postdoctoral Researcher / Research Fellow (2030–2033±) → Assistant Professor (2030s) → Associate Professor (mid/late 2030s) → Professor (late 2030s–2040s) → Senior Professor / Chair → Centre Director / Dean / Research Institute Leader

items.text: Postdoctoral research in environmental or climate law
Law-and-technology research focused on carbon markets, energy systems or environmental governance

blocks.text: At professor level, the objective shifts from accumulating qualifications to building an enduring research programme. Lead funded projects, supervise doctoral researchers, publish books and high-quality articles, participate in national and international policy discussions, develop a research centre or chair where appropriate, and keep teaching aligned with changes in environmental, energy and climate regulation. MoEFCC's current policy-and-law portfolio illustrates how quickly this area can expand into carbon markets, Paris Agreement Article 6, climate finance, environmental clearances and new environmental rules.
